/how-it-works.title: Meme Lab — How it works
/how-it-works.description: The complete Meme Lab journey: from a 30-reaction control to 3,000 searchable references, five ranked options, perspective matching, evaluation, and the path to 30,000.
/how-it-works.markdown:
HOW IT WORKS

# How Meme Lab finds the right reaction.

Meme Lab started as a controlled question: can a system understand a complete social situation well enough to choose the meme a person would actually send? This is the full journey—from the first dataset and failed approaches to the current retrieval, perspective, evaluation, and speed work.

 [Try the current version](/)

**Live now: 3,000 references · 6,000 vectors · five options** Full-sentence input · perspective matching · honest fit labels · serious-content guard

  PERSONAL TOOL

THE JOURNEY

## Each scale jump solved a different problem.

The catalogue did not jump straight to 3,000. Each stage stayed live, exposed a limitation, and supplied the evidence for the next stage.

01 · CONTROL **30 useful reactions**

The original release held 60 records: 30 reaction candidates and 30 caption templates. The picker deliberately used the 30 reactions as a small all-candidate control so every model choice could be inspected.

02 · COVERAGE **300 common references**

Two hundred and forty reviewed external records expanded the vocabulary. Vector retrieval replaced direct comparison, the collection became searchable, and the first public feedback loop went live.

03 · GENERALIZATION **1,000 broader references**

Seven hundred long-tail records forced dual-view retrieval, a fresh 60-case shadow set, a serious-content gate, and the first classifier bake-off. This is where Jev beat embedding-only ranking.

04 · SCALE **3,000 live references**

The first attempt hit the number by treating 1,189 public-domain artworks as reactions. The audit rejected that shortcut and replaced every artwork with a usage-backed reaction GIF.

05 · QUALITY **Five options, real viewpoints**

Complete sentence examples revealed that one situation can support the narrator’s reaction, the other person’s side, and the event itself. The UI now returns one primary choice and four visible backups across those angles.

06 · CALIBRATION **Labels instead of fake probability**

Jev’s old competitive score looked like a probability but was not one. A blind hard-case evaluation selected independent ordinal ratings, so the product now says weak, plausible, strong, or exact.

WHAT REAL USE CHANGED

## The product became simpler while the ranking became deeper.

The interface is intentionally one action: paste a complete comment and get a meme. The technical complexity stays behind that action.

Input

### Full sentences, not keywords

Examples describe the whole situation so actor roles, quoted speech, negation, relationship, and emotional tone survive retrieval.

Output

### One best choice plus four backups

The best result remains visually dominant. Four lower-ranked options stay visible because humour is subjective and several reactions can be valid.

Viewpoint

### My reaction, their side, the situation

Multi-person comments deliberately search all three angles instead of assuming every meme must speak only for the person who typed the comment.

Confidence

### Weak is shown honestly

A weak but usable option is labelled weak. The system abstains only when humour would be insensitive or every candidate would misrepresent the situation.

Interaction

### No generated explanation step

The user asked for a meme, not a paragraph. Removing live reasoning reduced latency and stopped plausible-sounding prose from disguising a mediocre match.

Feedback

### A small yes or no loop

One-tap feedback is retained for 30 days for evaluation. It does not silently retrain or overwrite the catalogue.

THE LIVE 3,000

## Retrieve. Compare. Return.

Every reference has a name, meaning, relational pattern, full-sentence example, near-miss, tags, provenance, media state, meme-strength score, and image-quality score. Runtime work stays bounded even as the catalogue grows.

- 01 **Validate and guard** Trim and bound the comment, treat it as untrusted text, and catch clear factual or serious help requests before joking.

- 02 **Retrieve 30** Embed the full comment, search meaning and usage-example vectors separately, then fuse both ranked lists.

- 03 **Compare by fit** Jev independently rates all 30 candidates. Multi-person comments also preserve explicit narrator, other-person, and situation lenses.

- 04 **Return five** Show one primary result and four backups labelled weak, plausible, strong, or exact. Persist only the bounded evaluation record.

THE RETRIEVAL SYSTEM

## 3,000 records never enter one prompt.

Vector search exists to find the plausible neighbourhood; the classifier decides which candidate is socially sendable. Meme strength and image quality remain separate so popularity never masquerades as contextual relevance.

COMMENT **Full situation**

2 SEARCHES **Meaning + usage**

FUSE **Top 30**

COMPARE **Best 5**

Workers AI

### One comment embedding

The same complete sentence queries two separately indexed views so abstract meaning and concrete usage can retrieve different useful candidates.

Vectorize

### 6,000 stored vectors

Three thousand references each contribute one meaning vector and one example vector. Reciprocal-rank fusion produces a unique shortlist of 30.

Core reserve

### Known-good coverage survives

Twenty shortlist slots search the full catalogue; ten reserve candidates from the original 1,000 so noisy expansion records cannot erase the stronger base.

Direct Jev

### Social fit beats keyword overlap

One structured TypeSafe request independently scores all 30 candidates. Full metadata lets Jev judge actors, target, tone, viewpoint, example, and near-miss instead of choosing the most familiar shared word.

Perspective mode

### Three lenses in one batch

One request selects distinct candidates for my reaction, their side, and the situation. A second request rates the selected five on the same ordinal scale before the UI orders them.

Failure policy

### No expensive fallback

If Jev is rate-limited, the product shows five semantic-retrieval matches as low-confidence weak fits. It never turns a traffic spike into unplanned 70B inference spend.

HOW 3,000 WAS BUILT

## The first 3,000 was wrong. The rebuild fixed the count.

A reusable image is not automatically a meme. The corrected catalogue keeps 1,805 named meme templates, removes empty editing canvases, and includes 1,195 reaction GIFs backed by observed conversational use.

**1,805** static meme templates

**1,195** reaction GIFs

**1.56M** observed reply pairs

**108+** uses per selected research GIF

**1,189** artwork fillers removed

**41** canonical memes tracked explicitly

- 01 **Require usage evidence** The GIF Reply research dataset contains 1.56 million real text-to-GIF reply pairs. Popularity comes from observed reactions, not visual guesswork.

- 02 **Keep stable provenance** Every GIF keeps its research hash, GIPHY ID, source page, direct media URL, preview URL, and observed-use count.

- 03 **Block unsafe and duplicate media** Source IDs, media URLs, normalized names, content tags, and duplicate checks prevent repeated or unsuitable records from padding the count.

- 04 **Track canonical gaps** A checked-in must-have list makes missing cultural staples visible. “My Name Is Jeff” is now a real GIF record, not an invisible omission.

- 05 **Keep strength separate from fit** Observed popularity influences meme strength. It never decides whether the reaction fits the sentence submitted right now.

- 06 **Write specific metadata locally** Local Qwen writes full meaning, social-dynamic, example, near-miss, and tag sentences. They remain assistant-authored pending owner feedback.

THE MODEL BAKE-OFF

## We tried fast models, local models, and smarter models.

No single model does everything. Embeddings discover candidates; Jev judges sendability; deterministic rules protect obvious serious cases; local models handled catalogue construction.

| Approach | Observed result | Speed | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | **Jev fast + full metadata** | 19/20 top-one in the enriched shortlist trial; strongest direct fit signal. | ~1.27s p95 on retrieved top 30 | LIVE |
 | **Rich ordinal Jev** | 9/12 exact first and 10/12 best-returned-first on the corrected hard set. | 1.60s p95 classifier stage | QUALITY WINNER |
 | **Compact ordinal Jev** | Same 9/12 exact first, but the best returned candidate ranked first on 9/12 instead of 10/12. | 1.20s p95 | SPEED FALLBACK |
 | **Llama 3.3 70B** | 80% top-three on 20 expansion cases; useful structure but unnecessary prose, slower responses, and unacceptable spike cost. | 3.85s p95 | REMOVED |
 | **BGE reranker** | 20% top-one and 45% top-three. It recognized topic similarity better than social sendability. | 1.83s p95 | NOT FINAL JUDGE |
 | **GLiNER 2.5** | 8/12 on meme-versus-none routing. Useful at extracting grief, emergency, authority, and tone features. | 52ms mean | FEATURE CANDIDATE |
 | **Laya** | 8/12 overall but 0/4 on meme cases. It routed too aggressively away from humour. | ~60ms median | RESEARCH ONLY |
 | **Qwen 3 4B local** | 66.7% routing accuracy and only 50% humour recall. Too conservative without tuning. | 2.45s p95 | NOT PROMOTED |
 | **Qwen 2.5 3B local** | 53.3% routing accuracy and 30% humour recall. Faster, but the quality loss was material. | 1.53s p95 | NOT PROMOTED |
 | **Jev smart** | No quality win over the fast ordinal approach. | 10.2–14.0s | TOO SLOW |

**Also tested**

Pairwise tournaments, calibration anchors, specificity-heavy prompts, a second-stage rerank of the first five, names-only metadata, and single-view retrieval.

**Not run**

Gemini structured output was not called because the repository has no bounded experiment credential. No result is claimed for it.

**The lesson**

More reasoning was not automatically better. Rich, specific candidate data plus an independently judged ordinal task was the strongest quality/cost combination.

THE EVALUATION LADDER

## One hundred broad cases plus twelve hard ranking cases.

The 100-case suite measures retrieval, ranking, and serious-content behavior across 75 humour and 25 no-meme situations. A separate 12-case hard set isolates the fit-score problem across 101 unique comment-and-candidate pairs.

- **Retrieval** Did an acceptable reference enter the top 30?

- **Top one / top three** Did ranking put a sendable choice near the front?

- **Abstention** Did serious requests avoid an inappropriate joke?

- **Calibration** Do weak, plausible, strong, and exact mean something consistent?

**Pre-ordinal 100-case snapshot:** retrieval reached 72% at 30, 67% top-one relevance, 71% top-three relevance, and 96% correct serious-content abstention. All labels remain pending owner review.

THE LATEST QUALITY DECISION

## Independent labels beat competitive probability.

The original Jev number was a probability inside a 30-way competition, not “the chance this meme is good.” We corrected a contradictory refrigerator fixture, rebuilt every arm, formed a 101-pair union, and had a fresh model rate the pairs blind to arm identity and scorer output.

OLD · RAW 30-WAY **7 / 12**

Exact first choice

**7 / 12**

Best returned candidate ranked first

 NDCG@5 0.895 · 1.27s p95

LIVE · RICH ORDINAL **9 / 12**

Exact first choice

**10 / 12**

Best returned candidate ranked first

 NDCG@5 0.950 · 1.60s p95

**Evidence boundary:** the blind rater was independent of the scoring outputs, but it was still a model—not human ground truth. These results justify the current engineering choice; owner feedback is still required before calling the labels calibrated.

SPEED RIGHT NOW

## Normal comments are near one to two seconds. Perspectives cost more.

Quality came first. These timings are observed remote-development requests from 21 September 2026, not a production SLA or a large benchmark.

SINGLE VIEW **0.98s**

“The tests finally passed after I changed nothing.”

SINGLE VIEW **1.88s**

“I looked for my phone while using its flashlight.”

THREE PERSPECTIVES **3.99s**

“My sibling ate the leftovers, then asked why I was upset.”

**The largest remaining slowdown**

Multi-person mode needs one batched perspective selection and one final ordinal rescore. Remote embedding, Vectorize, Jev networking, and D1 persistence add the remaining fixed costs.

**The safe optimization order**

First lock owner-reviewed quality. Then measure production p50/p95, trim metadata only when the same cases still pass, and avoid trading the recovered viewpoints away for a synthetic speed win.

STORAGE, MEDIA, AND COST

## The catalogue is stored. The media stays with its source.

The build pipeline is mostly local, but the live runtime is not completely local or free: it uses Cloudflare Workers AI, Vectorize, D1, and the direct TypeSafe Jev API.

CATALOGUE

### Versioned JSON and generated modules

Names, meanings, examples, near-misses, provenance, quality signals, and source URLs live with the project and generate the public collection.

SEMANTIC INDEX

### 6,000 vectors in Vectorize

Meaning and usage vectors are stored remotely so every request searches a bounded index instead of loading all 3,000 records.

MEDIA

### Provider-hosted images and GIFs

Imgflip, Memegen, and GIPHY assets load from recorded source URLs. Results animate GIFs; collection cards use lighter previews.

RIGHTS

### Usage evidence is not a licence

Research-backed popularity proves that a GIF is used as a reaction. It does not establish redistribution rights, so every external asset remains a labelled source preview.

FEEDBACK

### Bounded D1 records

The comment, returned candidate IDs, decision, labels, and yes/no feedback support evaluation and receive a 30-day expiry.

LOCAL WORK

### CLIP and Qwen built the collection

Uniqueness signals and long-form metadata were generated locally. The fastest local routing models tested so far were not accurate enough for the live decision.

WHAT WE STOPPED DOING

## The discarded ideas matter too.

This history prevents the project from repeating attractive experiments that already failed the quality, speed, or honesty bar.

- **Embeddings alone:** good for neighbourhoods, weak at deciding whether a reaction is socially sendable.

- **Generated reasoning on every result:** slower and unnecessary; fluent prose could make a poor selection sound convincing.

- **Raw Jev probability in the UI:** useful for competition ordering, misleading as user-facing confidence.

- **One perspective for every sentence:** lost valid reactions from the other participant or the situation itself.

- **Static meme strength as relevance:** a famous or high-quality image can still be the wrong response.

- **Jev smart and serial ensembles:** 5–14 second paths were too slow without a matching quality gain.

- **Current small local routers:** cheap and private, but too eager to abstain from genuine humour.

- **Claiming model labels as truth:** every metric remains visibly marked pending owner review.

- **Counting arbitrary artwork as memes:** the audit removed 1,189 public-domain images that had no evidence of meme use.

THE EXPANSION PLAN

## 30 → 300 → 1,000 → 3,000 → 30,000

3,000  references are live. Quality work now closes retrieval and perspective gaps before movie dialogue becomes a separate routed corpus.

**3,000 / 3,000 live** “I love you 3,000” is live.

    0  memes remaining ·  100 % complete

- 30 **Seed control** Inspectable all-candidate comparison and the first structured local experiment. _LIVE_

- 300 **Common reactions** Semantic retrieval, searchable collection, public feedback, and multi-option output. _LIVE_

- 1K **Broader vocabulary** Dual-view retrieval, classifier ranking, serious-content safety, and a fresh shadow evaluation. _LIVE_

- 3K **I love you 3,000** Uniqueness-gated acquisition, two vectors per record, five ordinal options, and explicit viewpoint coverage. _LIVE_

- 30K **Memes plus movie dialogue** Route the input to meme, dialogue, or none before corpus-specific retrieval. Keep evaluation and rights boundaries separate for each corpus. _NEXT CORPUS_

**1. Owner-label the hard set**

Confirm the ordinal winner and calibrate what weak, plausible, strong, and exact actually mean.

**2. Close retrieval misses**

The stage-3,000 snapshot found a usable candidate in the retrieved 30 on 72% of broad cases. Ranking cannot rescue a candidate it never sees.

**3. Compress perspective latency**

Replace four classifier interactions only after a one-call design proves equal viewpoint coverage on replayable cases.

**4. Add the 30,000 router**

Evaluate meme, dialogue, ambiguous, and none slices independently before combining their output in one product.

THE RULE THAT SURVIVED EVERY STAGE

## Bigger is useful only if the results stay honest.

Three thousand is live, not “finished.” The corrected set contains meme templates and usage-backed reaction GIFs only. Metadata and evaluation labels still need owner review, source previews do not imply media rights, and a weak match stays visibly weak.

/privacy.title: Meme Lab — Privacy
/privacy.description: How Meme Lab handles comments, feedback and optional forms.
/privacy.markdown:
# Privacy

Meme Lab uses your submitted comment to retrieve and rank meme references. Matching and caption generation send the situation and relevant reference information to the configured AI service. Avoid submitting sensitive personal information.

## Comments and feedback

Your comment and returned candidate IDs and scores are kept for 30 days to support feedback and evaluation. Landed or missed feedback is linked to that recommendation. Expired recommendations and their linked feedback are removed by scheduled cleanup.

## Caption editor and previews

Caption editing, PNG rendering and captioned video export happen in your browser. Gallery caption generation sends your situation, optional audience, caption style, selected reference and three small preview frames from the chosen clip to the configured AI service; gallery situations and drafts are not stored by Meme Lab. Reaction clips are fetched from their recorded source through Meme Lab for preview and export. Source previews may load from external media hosts, which receive ordinary network request information. Media rights are not established unless a licensed source is identified.

## Optional forms and diagnostics

The optional newsletter and site feedback forms send the information you choose to provide to SaaS Maker. Their handling is described in [SaaS Maker’s privacy policy](https://sassmaker.com/privacy). App diagnostics record bounded event and performance information, including the existing recommendation ID, result rank, feedback outcome and whether an image download was requested or failed. Diagnostic events do not include your comment or caption text. A download request does not confirm that a file was saved or used.

[Back to Meme Lab](/)

/anna-privacy.markdown:
# Meme Lab on Anna

Privacy and source information. Updated 5 October 2026.

## What happens to your comment

When you choose Find the meme inside Anna, your situation is sent to the Meme Lab search service at memes.significanthobbies.com. The service uses Cloudflare Workers AI and Vectorize to find relevant catalogue references. The shortlist endpoint does not save your comment or write feedback to Meme Lab’s database.

Your situation and the retrieved reference metadata are then sent through Anna to your Anna-configured AI provider for ranking. For editable caption drafts, your situation and selected template metadata also go to Meme Lab’s stateless caption-planning endpoint, then through Anna to your AI provider. Templates without inspected caption regions send their source image URL to that provider for placement. The caption-planning endpoint does not store your situation or run AI itself. Anna and the provider process requests under their own policies, including any retention they apply. Meme Lab does not claim those services have zero retention. Avoid including private or sensitive information in a situation.

## Permissions and cost

The Anna edition requests AI completion access. It also requests access to its own per-user Anna storage for saved reference IDs/names and the day of your last visit. The personalized-meme edition also requests image generation, explicit image uploads and file operations in its own per-user Anna app storage. It does not request chat history, credentials, other apps’ storage, camera or microphone access. AI requests may consume your Anna credits or BYOK provider quota; file uploads and private saved creations also use Anna storage quota. There is no separate Meme Lab subscription.

## Saved reactions and measurement

Saving a reaction stores only its catalogue ID and name in your own Meme Lab storage bucket on Anna. It never saves your situation. Saved entries remain until you remove them; Anna governs the underlying storage and retention. A last-visit day supports a repeat-visit counter.

Allowlisted interaction event names—for successful matches, abstentions, errors, copied/shared links, saved/removed references, created/saved remixes, download starts, image shares and repeat visits—are sent to Meme Lab for aggregate operational logging in Cloudflare and App Health. These events contain no situation, email, user ID, provider key or persistent tracking identifier. They are client-reported interactions, not verified unique people or earnings. Anna separately records its authenticated app and AI-session activity under its own policies.

The search and event endpoints apply endpoint-specific burst limits using the network IP address as a Cloudflare limiter key. Shared network users share this limit. It does not identify your Anna account or impose an exact global spending cap.

## Source previews and sharing

Images and GIFs load directly from their external source providers, including Imgflip, Memegen and Giphy. Those providers receive the normal network request information needed to serve a preview. Source provenance and observed conversational use do not establish redistribution rights. Catalogue caption drafts retain source-preview labels. The separate personalized-meme editor lets you supply an image you can edit and a photo you have permission to use.

Sharing copies a stable public reference link containing its catalogue ID. Your submitted comment is never added to that link. Supported static references can open as editable caption drafts. Their source images load through Meme Lab’s allowlisted media proxy. Downloading explicitly saves the finished captioned PNG privately in Anna before Anna opens the download. Drafts stay in the current tab; source provenance does not establish redistribution or transformation rights. Source previews may become unavailable; the reference name remains visible when a preview fails.

## Uploaded photos and personal memes

When you choose Generate my meme, the selected photo and meme image are decoded and re-encoded in your browser to remove embedded metadata, then uploaded to Anna’s R2 storage and sent to your Anna-configured image provider. Meme Lab’s Cloudflare search service does not receive these images, their URLs or image-generation prompts. Anna and the provider govern processing and retention. Clearing the editor removes local previews; it does not promise deletion of images already uploaded to those services.

One requested image is generated per attempt. There is no automatic retry or separate paid-provider fallback. Generated images may change captions, likeness, expression or background; compare the result with the original before sharing. Animated images are not supported. No face recognition or identity verification is performed.

Save to Anna stores only the generated PNG privately in your own Meme Lab file storage. Download also saves the generated PNG there so Anna’s host can open the browser download outside the app frame. Your input photo and situation are not copied into that saved-creation library. Saved outputs persist until you remove them. Removal soft-deletes the saved output, with physical object cleanup governed by Anna’s storage reaper; it does not remove prior recipient copies or source uploads.

Sharing a personal meme attaches its generated image file to your browser’s share chooser where supported. It is an explicit action, with no automatic publication or public gallery. When direct file sharing is unavailable, download the PNG and attach it yourself. File URLs are temporary signed handles, not permanent public share links. Download-start and client share events do not prove recipient delivery or qualified users.

## The public website is a separate workflow

If you follow a reference link to the public Meme Lab website and use its composer, that website retains comments and returned candidates for 30 days to support its feedback workflow. This retention does not apply to the Anna shortlist endpoint.

## Questions

Report product problems through [Meme Lab’s support issues](https://github.com/Significant-Hobbies/meme-lab/issues). Do not post a private comment in a public issue. Read [Anna’s privacy policy](https://anna.partners/legal/privacy) for platform processing.

## what meme lab actually does

Meme Lab is a personal meme picker. You paste a complete comment or describe a situation — a group-chat argument, a workplace absurdity, a small domestic injustice — and it returns the one meme that fits it best, followed by four honestly ranked alternatives. Every result carries an ordinal fit label and an honest confidence level, so a weak match says it is weak instead of pretending otherwise.

## the catalogue behind it

The recommendations draw on a corrected 3,000-reference catalogue: 1,805 named meme templates and 1,195 reaction GIFs chosen because real conversations actually used them — each selected GIF has at least 108 observed replies in the GIF Reply research dataset. Every reference records what it expresses, the social dynamic it captures, an example of where it fits, and a near-miss case where it would be wrong. You can browse all of it in the [collection](/collection).

## how matching works

Your comment is compared against two embedding views of the catalogue — one indexed by meaning, one by example — then the shortlist is scored on five ordered fit levels. Comments that involve more than one person are answered from three angles: your reaction, their side, and the situation itself. Serious requests — condolences, apologies, safety, anything that needs a real answer — are declined before humour is considered; no meme is the right meme there. The full methodology, including how results are evaluated, lives on [how it works](/how-it-works).
